within 24 hours answers the first response again, with

automatic.description: True for the comparison Examen keeps of a candidate against its experiment's reference.

baseline.description: The baseline record the reference side reads, when it is one.

candidate_suite.description: Per metric, the candidate's own suite-level summary over the tasks of its suite with weight greater than zero.

confounds.description: The name of every confound of its results.

declaration.description: For a declared comparison of the general form, its declaration: the cell variable it compares, its two levels, where and by, and the metric of its primary result.

declared.description: For a comparison its experiment declared, its position in the experiment's comparisons; absent otherwise.

declared_provenance.description: The sides, candidate and reference, whose candidate is of kind external, so whose tuple its harness declared.

exploratory.description: True for a comparison computed on request, and for an automatic one against a reference set after a cell left pending: it is never headlined.

final.description: True once both sides are final; false while a figure can still change.

inputs_digest.description: The digest of its inputs document.

reference_candidate.description: The reference candidate's digest, when the reference side is a candidate.

reference_task.description: For a comparison across tasks, the reference task.

results.description: Its results; GET /comparisons/{id} answers the suite-level and candidate-level ones, and /rows the task-level ones.

single_variable.description: No tuple field besides variable differs on any paired task; absent until computed.

task.description: For a comparison across tasks, the candidate's task.

taxonomies.description: For each open-vocabulary metric it reads, the id of the taxonomy record its canonical labels were read at.

variable.description: The tuple fields the comparison intends to vary.

verdict_counts.description: Per metric, the number of task-level results with each verdict.

Confound.description: One confound of a result: a field besides the variable compared in which the two sides differ, or a condition of the trials the result read.

candidate.description: Per side: a count of requests or trials, a window {from, to}, or a taxonomy record id, by the confound's name; absent for a tuple field.

grader.description: For uncalibrated, the judge version whose calibration the result read.

reference.description: As candidate, for the reference side.

tasks.description: On a suite-level result, the task names it applies to.

Correction.description: The correction applied to the comparison's p-values.

declared.description: On a declared comparison, the size of the declared family its primary result is corrected in.

family.description: How many p-values the one corrected family held.

primary.description: The digest of the metric whose primary result is out of the family, tested alone and reported uncorrected, or for a declared comparison corrected in the declared family; absent on an exploratory comparison.

independence.description: The experiment's test of independence when it declares one: its declaration, its levels, their summaries, its strata, the test and its p, verdict and reason; before any cell holds a finished trial, its declaration, levels and reason alone.

message.description: The one sentence a person reads, the same for every occurrence of the code.

ErrorCode.description: Every code a client branches on.

constant.description: The limit a request exceeds, on `limit_exceeded`.

core.description: The core an error is about.

detail.description: The developer detail, on every error but `internal`.

field.description: The member or parameter the error is about, as a dotted path with indexes.

fields.description: The fields that differ or are not pinned, on `provenance_mismatch`.

figure.description: The figure a limit holds, on a `forbidden` a limit made.

reason.description: One snake_case word for this instance.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed later unchanged.

state.description: The object's state, on a conflict with it.

budget.description: The Lux Budget the experiment is metered against, and its figures as the key source read them when the answer was built, reused for at most BUDGET_STATUS_TTL. The figures are absent when no key source answered them, or carry currency in their place for a Budget in another currency than USD.

remaining_usd_micro.description: The smallest remainder across the Budget and every Budget that pays for it, in micro-USD.

spent_usd_micro.description: What the Budget spent, in micro-USD.

comparisons.description: The comparisons the experiment declared at create, each candidate and task by digest.

by.description: The general form: the cell variables the comparison is stratified by; without it, each side is one cell.

levels.description: The general form: the variable's two levels, the candidate side's first. A candidate's level is its digest and a task's its name or digest.

metric.description: The metric whose result is the comparison's primary result, by digest; absent when it is the suite's primary metric.

variable.description: On a pair of candidates, one logical variable: agent, model, reasoning, tools, environment or workspace. In the general form, the cell variable compared: candidate, task, model, reasoning or a task factor's name.

where.description: The general form: cell variables each held to one level.

created_by.description: The subject that created the experiment, set at create and never changed. It differs from `owner` for an experiment created in an organization's context, where the owner is the organization and this is the member.

independence.description: The experiment's test of independence, its metric by digest and its defaults filled. Fixed at create; absent when the experiment declares none.

owner.description: Whose the experiment is: the owner context its create resolved, a person or an organization, as the authorizer names it.

usage.description: On a read of one experiment whose runs hold the experiment's Key: what Lux recorded of the calls made with it. unattributed counts the calls no trial claims by its request label or a submitted request id, which count toward the experiment and no trial. read_to is how far the records were read.

cost_usd_micro.description: The priced calls' cost, in micro-USD.

unpriced_requests.description: The calls Lux could not price, whose cost is unknown.

comparisons.description: The comparisons the experiment declares it will make, at most MAX_DECLARED_COMPARISONS: a pair of candidates with an optional variable; one candidate's two tasks by name or digest; or the general form, a cell variable, its two levels, and optional where and by. Each form takes an optional metric. Each is computed without being asked and is not exploratory, and their primary results are corrected together. Fixed at create.

by.description: The general form: the cell variables the comparison is stratified by; without it, each side is one cell.

levels.description: The general form: the variable's two levels, the candidate side's first. A candidate's level is its digest and a task's its name or digest.

metric.description: The metric whose result is the comparison's primary result, by name or digest; the suite's primary metric when absent.

variable.description: On a pair of candidates, one logical variable: agent, model, reasoning, tools, environment or workspace. In the general form, the cell variable compared: candidate, task, model, reasoning or a task factor's name.

where.description: The general form: cell variables each held to one level.

independence.description: The experiment's test of independence: a trial-level label metric of the suite, by name or digest, against a cell variable, `candidate` when absent, stratified by the cell variables of `by`, over the cells `where` selects. `by` is `["task"]` when absent for a variable of the candidate and `["candidate"]` for the task or a factor. Fixed at create.

scheduling.description: How the experiment's cells take its parallelism and its external trials are leased: `task_by_task`, the default, a task's cells before the next task's, or `interleaved`, every cell of every task in turn, so trial i of every cell runs in one window. Fixed at create.

sign_in.description: An opaque value the client's installation gave it for this create, such as a handle to a sign-in the installation keeps for the experiment. Examen passes it to the authorizer as sign_in on experiment.create and keeps it nowhere: it is not stored on the experiment, answered, logged or sent in an event.

preamble.description: Examen's judge preamble, pinned on the grader at apply and covered by its digest. A body may leave it out or send it as answered; any other text is refused.

checks.description: Read the values the trial's checks recorded, by metric name, as one block, once every check of the trial ended.

LabelShare.description: One label's count and proportion in a distribution, with the proportion's interval.

unmapped.description: A raw label of an open vocabulary the taxonomy record read does not map.

model_key.description: The experiment's Lux Key, which each trial's model calls go through so the experiment's Budget binds them and Lux's records of them are the trial's cost. Absent when the installation has no key source. The answer is sent with Cache-Control: no-store, and no other answer carries the Key.

candidate.description: The candidate the trial runs, with the configuration its harness declared.

lux_labels.description: The value of the Lux-Labels header each of the trial's model calls carries, examen.trial=<trial id>, which attributes the call to the trial.

candidate.description: An external candidate of the experiment; absent, the lease takes trials of every external candidate.

LeftOut.description: A task of weight above zero that a suite-level result does not include, with each side's valued trials.

Parameters.description: The values the comparison was computed with.

Resamples.description: PERMUTATION_RESAMPLES as resolved for the primary result and for the family.

Result.description: One result of a comparison, as the analysis computed it.

delta.description: The change, candidate less reference: a number, or for a label metric an object from each label to the difference of its proportions.

delta_interval.description: The delta's interval at CONFIDENCE_LEVEL, for per_label an object from each label to its interval; absent where none is computed.

exact.description: Whether the test enumerated every case.

h.description: On a pair result of two benchmark entries, the Holm-adjusted value, in place of q; absent on a comparison's result.

left_out.description: On a suite-level result, each task of weight above zero the result does not include.

level.description: task, over one task's cells; suite, over the paired tasks it includes; or candidate, a candidate-level metric's one value per side, which is descriptive.

method.description: The test: boschloo_exact, permutation, stratified_permutation, fisher_freeman_halton or chi_square_permutation; absent on a descriptive result.

no_delta_interval.description: When delta_interval is absent on a result that is not insufficient, one plain sentence saying why.

q.description: The value after the correction at FALSE_DISCOVERY_RATE.

reason.description: One plain sentence saying why the verdict is what it is.

resamples.description: How many relabelings or tables the test enumerated or drew; absent for boschloo_exact.

statistic.description: The statistic the test orders by: fisher_p, welch_t, studentized_quantile, difference, table_probability, pearson_x2 or pearson_x2_sum; absent on a descriptive result.

task.description: On a task-level result, the task's name; for a comparison across tasks, both names joined by ` vs `; for a declared comparison of the general form, its stratum's name.

task_digests.description: On a task-level result, each side's task digest.

Summary.description: One metric over one set of trials: a cell, or a candidate's tasks at suite level.

aggregate.description: The metric's aggregate; absent for a candidate-level metric.

coverage.description: At suite level, the share of the suite's weight the included tasks hold.

denominator.description: The finished trials holding a current value of the metric, less those exclude_labels leaves out.

distribution.description: For a label metric, each label's count and proportion.

excluded.description: The trials of the set not counted in n, by reason: retried, infra_failed, over_budget, canceled or not_done.

excluded_labels.description: For a cell-level metric, the valued trials its exclude_labels left out, by label.

final.description: True once every declared trial of the set is done and graded; false while the figure can still change.

missing.description: n less denominator, and for a cell-level metric less the trials excluded_labels counts.

mode.description: For a label metric, its most frequent label.

n.description: The finished trials of the set that the metric applies to.

no_interval.description: When interval is absent, one plain sentence saying why.

not_applicable.description: The finished trials outside the metric's applies_to, in neither n nor missing.

numerator.description: For rate, the finished trials whose value is true; for mode_share, the trials holding the most frequent label.

tasks.description: At suite level, the number of tasks included.

unmapped.description: For an open-vocabulary metric, the finished trials whose raw label the taxonomy record read does not map.

value.description: The rate, mean, median or p90; for distribution, an object from each label to its share; for repeat_rate, mode_share and distinct_count, the statistic; for a candidate-level metric, its one current value. Absent when nothing is valued.

factors.description: The task's place in a design: each factor's name to the task's level of it, at most MAX_TASK_FACTORS. Declared comparisons and a test of independence select and stratify cells by them.

graders.description: Judges and annotation queues by digest, applied to this task's trials alone beside the suite's graders.

checks.description: One check run record per check of the task, in order: {grader, state, exit_code, reason, duration, stdout_size, stdout_sha256, stderr_tail, image, sandbox, generation, outputs}; state is pending until the run ended; sandbox is the id of the check sandbox it ran in, which Cella removes once the trial's checks end. outputs, for a check that ran, are its standard output and standard error as Examen kept them in the owner's files store, each an evidence reference {kind: check_output, name: stdout.txt or stderr.txt, owner, path, digest, size} under files/evals/experiments/<experiment>/cells/<cell>/trials/<trial>/checks/<grader hex>/; absent where the store did not take them.

judgments.description: One judgment record per model judge of the trial: {grader, generation, state, attempts, request_digest, cuts, boundary, served_model, tokens, cost_usd_micro, reason}; state is pending until the judgment ended.

observed.description: What happened in the trial. From Lux's records of its calls: served (the models that served them, each with its count), input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_state (known, unpriced when a call was not priced, or unknown when no record of the trial was read) and cost_usd when known. For a topos trial, machines: each machine its session ran on, {kind, id}, once, in the order its log attached them, such as {kind: cella, id: sbx_...} for a Cella sandbox.

sent.description: What the trial's model calls named, from Lux's records of the calls made with the experiment's Key: how many it made, and one entry per distinct model and reasoning level. Absent until those records are read, and for a trial no record of which carries its label or a request id it submitted.

values.description: On a list's items: each trial-level metric's current value by name, null for none.

UnpairedTasks.description: The task names one side holds alone.

Version.description: A version: its kind's fields as applied, beside its record.

Window.description: A side's time window: the earliest started_at and the latest ended_at of the trials read.

Windows.description: Each side's window over every trial the comparison read; a side that read none has none.

bearer.description: A token of an issuer EXAMEN_OIDC_ISSUERS names, addressed to an audience EXAMEN_OIDC_AUDIENCE names.

info.description:
A client applies tasks, suites, candidates and the metrics and graders
they are measured by, runs experiments over them, and reads cells,
trials, measurements and comparisons that come back already computed.
Every route but this document takes a bearer token of an issuer the
server trusts, and every route asks the server's authorizer before it
acts. An object the caller may not see reads as a missing one.

This document describes the routes the running release serves; a route
of a later build step is added in the release that serves it.

Every error is one object: a `code` to branch on, a fixed `message`
for a person, and `details` for a developer. A request with a member
this document does not describe is `400 unknown_field`, a body longer
than the request bound is `413 request_too_large`, and every `429`
carries `Retry-After` in whole seconds. A list answers
`{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}`, with `next_cursor` absent on
the last page. A create that takes an `Idempotency-Key` answers a
repeat of the same key and body with the first response and
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

The probes `GET /livez`, `GET /readyz` and `GET /version` sit outside
the base path on the same listener and take no token.

Candidates of kind `external` and `topos` run; a candidate of kind `program` is `422 executor_unavailable`. A `topos` candidate needs an installation that starts Topos sessions, else `422 core_not_configured`; one that names `tools`, and a task it runs that names an environment or an Arca workspace, are `422 executor_unavailable`, and a task it runs without an instruction is `422 missing_field`.
